outlook.summary: Not financial advice — this is a personal tracking dashboard meant to organize publicly available information for research purposes. Always size positions and confirm with your own research.

strongest.area: Chips & AI hardware, led by Micron, AMD, ASML and Arm
strongest.reason: AI-chip demand signals stayed resilient across the board even as OpenAI's newly unveiled in-house inference chip raised fresh competitive questions, with continued fund rotation into foundry, memory and IP leaders

strongest.area: AI infrastructure buildout, led by Nvidia, Broadcom and Oracle
strongest.reason: hyperscaler 2026 capex guidance climbed to a combined $775-800B, underpinning demand even as scrutiny grows over hyperscalers now spending roughly 102% of cloud revenue on capex

weakest.area: Cybersecurity software, led by Zscaler and CrowdStrike
weakest.reason: Zscaler's soft FY2027 growth guidance overshadowed an otherwise clean earnings beat and triggered a sector-wide selloff that dragged peers lower alongside it

weakest.area: Robotics-adjacent names, led by Intuitive Surgical and Tesla
weakest.reason: Intuitive Surgical faces a fresh competitive threat after the FDA authorized Johnson & Johnson's Ottava robotic-surgery platform, while Tesla continues digesting Cybercab and NHTSA fallout alongside broader AI/robotics capex concerns

outlook.nextStep: The August CPI report (Sept 11) and the Sept 15-16 FOMC decision remain the dominant catalysts worth tracking closely, given how much rate-hike odds have swung on individual Fed comments. Zscaler's guidance-driven cybersecurity selloff and JNJ's Ottava authorization are worth a closer look for follow-through over the next few sessions, while Tesla's regulatory overhang and Adobe's pre-earnings jitters are probably better watched than acted on given how much uncertainty is already priced in ahead of Wednesday's report.

signals.title: Fed rate call stays a coin flip ahead of key CPI report
signals.body: Views remain split heading into the Sept 15-16 FOMC meeting: some desks see a hold as Fed Governor Waller cites cooling inflation, while J.P. Morgan Wealth Management strategists now expect a 25bp hike tied to energy-driven supply-chain shocks. The August CPI report due Sept 11 is the single biggest near-term swing factor.
signals.focus: the most important date on the calendar this month worth tracking closely; day-to-day comment-driven swings are probably better watched than traded on

signals.title: Zscaler's soft guidance triggers a broad cybersecurity retreat
signals.body: Zscaler beat on earnings but guided FY2027 revenue growth to just 17%, a sharp deceleration from fiscal 2026's roughly 25% pace, sending its shares down sharply and pulling CrowdStrike and other sector peers lower in sympathy even without company-specific news of their own.
signals.focus: a growth-deceleration scare worth watching for whether other names confirm the slowdown or diverge at their own upcoming reports

signals.title: JNJ's Ottava gets FDA authorization, a new rival for Intuitive Surgical
signals.body: The FDA granted marketing authorization to Johnson & Johnson's Ottava platform, marking JNJ's entry into soft-tissue robotic surgery and a direct challenge to the da Vinci franchise that anchors Intuitive Surgical's business, on top of already slowing U.S. procedure growth.
signals.focus: a structural competitive threat worth a closer look rather than a one-day headline to react to

signals.title: OpenAI's in-house inference chip raises questions for merchant AI silicon
signals.body: OpenAI unveiled a custom AI inference chip, code-named 'Jalapeno,' reportedly showing industry-leading performance and signaling a strategic push toward greater infrastructure control, adding to a broader theme of hyperscalers and top AI labs building their own silicon alongside merchant suppliers like Nvidia and AMD.
signals.focus: a slow-building competitive dynamic worth watching over quarters, not something the current AI-chip rally suggests markets are pricing in yet

signals.title: Hyperscaler capex hits 102% of cloud revenue, sharpening ROI scrutiny
signals.body: Amazon, Alphabet and Microsoft are together on pace to spend roughly 102% of their cloud revenue on capex in 2026, recycling nearly all cloud income back into AI infrastructure, with the top five hyperscalers guiding to $775-800B combined for the year. Microsoft stands out with strong free cash flow despite the spending pace, while Alphabet and Meta have shown weaker free-cash-flow trends.
signals.focus: a valuable gauge of AI-spending durability worth tracking each earnings cycle rather than reacting to on any single data point

signals.title: Adobe's CEO transition overshadows Wednesday's earnings
signals.body: Adobe shares stayed pressured as investors continued weighing the incoming CEO transition (Anil Chakravarthy succeeds Shantanu Narayen in December) just two days ahead of its Sept 10 earnings report. Analyst opinion remains split, with some flagging AI-substitution risk to Creative Cloud and others raising price targets.
signals.focus: a genuine fork in analyst opinion worth watching resolve at Wednesday's report rather than reacting to the transition headline alone

signals.title: Crypto stays soft as CPI report approaches
signals.body: Bitcoin and Ether both eased further, extending a cooldown from August's strong spot-ETF-driven rally as the broader crypto market stayed cautious heading into next week's CPI print and the Fed's rate decision.
signals.focus: a reminder of how sensitive crypto remains to Fed expectations; probably better watched through the Sept 11 CPI print than traded on daily swings
